title: Migration header says erasure 'removes the row', contradicting the tombstone design documented in the same file
evidence:
Line 12-13: '--   * Erasure — the continue email carries a self-service delete link
--     (POST /apply/:code/draft-erasure/:token) that removes the row.'
vs line 41-46: '-- Erasure tombstone: a confirmed Art. 17 deletion wipes fields/token but
-- keeps the (vacancy, email) key until vacancy close so a still-open form
-- tab's next auto-save hits the upsert's erased_at guard instead of
-- silently re-creating the PII payload.' — and server/src/application/sql/erase_draft_by_token.sql confirms: 'tombstone, NOT a hard delete ... the (vacancy, email) key is kept as a suppression record until the retention sweep removes it at vacancy close' (UPDATE ... SET fields = '{}', continue_token = NULL, erased_at = now()).
detail: Stale pre-W3 comment: the spec change log (Perkins r1, W3) changed erasure to a tombstone that keeps the (vacancy, email) key until vacancy close, but the header bullet still claims the endpoint removes the row. Comment-only, but it misstates the GDPR erasure semantics of the table it documents.
recommended_fix: Reword the header bullet to match the tombstone, e.g. 'Erasure — the continue email carries a self-service delete link (POST /apply/:code/draft-erasure/:token) that wipes fields/token and tombstones the row (see erased_at); the retention sweep removes the key at vacancy close.'
